sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马斯。

sentences.en: Hey, how are you?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你好吗？

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Good, good.
sentences.zh: 很好，很好。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Imagine you're in a hospital room, waiting to hear the results of a test you had.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你正坐在医院的病房里，等待着检查结果。

sentences.en: The doctor comes in.
sentences.zh: 医生走了进来。

sentences.en: I know last time you were here two weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 我知道你上次来是两周前。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: One of the things that we did was perform a colonoscopy.
sentences.zh: 我们当时做的一项检查是结肠镜检查。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was not fun.
sentences.zh: 是的，那次体验不太好。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You might sense, on some level, what's about to happen.
sentences.zh: 你可能在某种程度上预感到了即将发生什么。

sentences.en: You know, I got the results back and reviewed them with Dr. Liu.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我拿到了结果，并和刘医生一起复核了。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is kind of difficult for me to say because, unfortunately, I have some bad news to tell you.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这对我来说有点难以启齿，因为很遗憾，我有一些坏消息要告诉你。

sentences.en: The muscles in your shoulders tense up.
sentences.zh: 你的肩膀肌肉紧绷起来。

sentences.en: Your hands suddenly feel clammy.
sentences.zh: 你的手心突然冒汗。

sentences.en: They found a mass in your descending colon.
sentences.zh: 他们在你的降结肠发现了一个肿块。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And so they did a biopsy.
sentences.zh: 所以他们做了活检。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And what a biopsy does, it lets us know what kind of cells there are to see if it's positive for cancer.
sentences.zh: 活检的作用是让我们了解细胞的类型，看看是否呈癌症阳性。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And then you get some very bad news.
sentences.zh: 然后你得到了非常糟糕的消息。

sentences.en: The results came back that it is an invasive adenocarcinoma.
sentences.zh: 结果显示是浸润性腺癌。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And what that means is that you do have colon cancer.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你确实患有结肠癌。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: The cancer is basically untreatable.
sentences.zh: 这种癌症基本上无法治疗。

sentences.en: When the cancer is this far advanced, there is no hope.
sentences.zh: 当癌症发展到这个阶段，已经没有希望了。

sentences.en: I'm very sorry to give you this news.
sentences.zh: 很抱歉告诉你这个消息。

sentences.en: I know it's not what you were expecting.
sentences.zh: 我知道这不是你所预期的。

sentences.en: It's very, uh...
sentences.zh: 这非常，呃……

sentences.en: Then, after about 10 minutes, a timer goes off.
sentences.zh: 然后，大约10分钟后，计时器响了。

sentences.en: And the encounter is over.
sentences.zh: 会面结束了。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Please feel free to call.
sentences.zh: 请随时打电话。

sentences.en: Okay, everyone, take a deep breath.
sentences.zh: 好了，各位，深呼吸。

sentences.en: That was not actually somebody being told they had terminal cancer.
sentences.zh: 那并不是真的有人被告知患了绝症。

sentences.en: It was part of an exam for med students at Rush Medical College in Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这是芝加哥拉什医学院为医学生准备的考试的一部分。

sentences.en: I do remember that student, and I thought he did a really, really nice job.
sentences.zh: 我记得那个学生，我觉得他表现得非常、非常好。

sentences.en: That's Mark Parra.
sentences.zh: 那是马克·帕拉。

sentences.en: He played the patient.
sentences.zh: 他扮演病人。

sentences.en: He went the whole day being told by medical students that he was dying and then reacting as if that was actually happening.
sentences.zh: 他整天都在听医学生说他快死了，然后还要做出仿佛这一切正在真实发生的反应。

sentences.en: It's, yeah, it's difficult.
sentences.zh: 这，是的，这很困难。

sentences.en: It's a long day.
sentences.zh: 这是漫长的一天。

sentences.en: It's a long day.
sentences.zh: 这是漫长的一天。

sentences.en: It's a little like a demented theme park job.
sentences.zh: 这有点像是在疯狂主题公园里的工作。

sentences.en: But as difficult as it is, Mark is playing an important role for med students like Artie Naziri.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此困难，马克还是为像阿蒂·纳齐里这样的医学生扮演了一个重要的角色。

sentences.en: It's never a good feeling to break bad news to patients, but I understand that no matter which field I go into or which specialty,
sentences.zh: 向病人传达坏消息从来都不是一种好的感觉，但我明白，无论我进入哪个领域或哪个专业，

sentences.en: this is something that we all will have to endure at some point.
sentences.zh: 这都是我们所有人迟早要面对的事情。

sentences.en: In medicine, bad news is defined as any information that drastically and negatively alters a patient's outlook for the future.
sentences.zh: 在医学上，坏消息被定义为任何会剧烈且负面地改变病人未来前景的信息。

sentences.en: John Fasile is a radio reporter and part-time medical school videographer.
sentences.zh: 约翰·法西尔是一位广播记者，也是兼职医学院摄像师。

sentences.en: He actually set up cameras to film that encounter between Mark and Artie so that Artie could be evaluated on his communication skills.
sentences.zh: 他实际上架设了摄像机来拍摄马克和阿蒂之间的那次会面，以便评估阿蒂的沟通技巧。

sentences.en: And I was really surprised by how calm and compassionate Artie was.
sentences.zh: 我对阿蒂表现出的冷静和同情心感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: Many doctors struggle with breaking bad news.
sentences.zh: 许多医生在传达坏消息时都很挣扎。

sentences.en: I've heard stories about a doctor leaving a voicemail to tell a patient she had cancer.
sentences.zh: 我听说过有医生通过语音留言告诉病人她患了癌症的故事。

sentences.en: And I heard another story about a doctor who used a sports analogy to deliver difficult information.
sentences.zh: 我还听说过另一个医生用体育比喻来传达困难信息的故事。

sentences.en: As in, it's the bottom of the ninth and there's one out left.
sentences.zh: 比如，比赛到了九局下半，还剩下一个出局数。

sentences.en: Breaking bad news is as delicate a procedure as any surgery.
sentences.zh: 传达坏消息和任何外科手术一样，都是一项精细的操作。

sentences.en: And there can be serious consequences if things go wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果处理不当，可能会产生严重的后果。

sentences.en: If the patient doesn't understand their diagnosis or what the next steps are,
sentences.zh: 如果病人不了解他们的诊断结果或接下来的步骤，

sentences.en: they could end up making uninformed decisions about their treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们最终可能会在不了解情况的情况下做出关于治疗的决定。

sentences.en: Which is why many medical schools now offer training.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么许多医学院现在提供相关培训的原因。

sentences.en: They bring in actors to help students learn how to navigate this critically important and very high-stakes moment.
sentences.zh: 他们请来演员帮助学生学习如何应对这一至关重要且风险极高的时刻。

sentences.en: A moment that most of us will experience one way or another.
sentences.zh: 一个我们大多数人迟早都会以某种方式经历的时刻。

sentences.en: But that's not the only connection between acting and this particular facet of medicine.
sentences.zh: 但这并不是表演与医学这一特定层面之间的唯一联系。

sentences.en: Over the last, you know, 20 or 30 years, there have been endless anecdotes just as you described.
sentences.zh: 在过去，你知道，20或30年里，有无数像你描述的那样的轶事。

sentences.en: The doctor came in and said, you'll be dead Friday, goodbye, and left.
sentences.zh: 医生走进来，说你周五就会死，再见，然后就走了。

sentences.en: It turns out one of the first doctors to recognize this problem, he wasn't just a physician.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，最早认识到这个问题的一位医生，他不仅仅是一位内科医生。

sentences.en: He was also a comedian.
sentences.zh: 他也是一位喜剧演员。

sentences.en: And he actually drew on that experience to transform the way that doctors break bad news.
sentences.zh: 他实际上利用了那种经验来改变医生传达坏消息的方式。

sentences.en: There are ways of doing this.
sentences.zh: 这样做是有方法的。

sentences.en: There are ways of breaking bad news.
sentences.zh: 传达坏消息是有方法的。

sentences.en: His name was Rob Buckman.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫罗伯·巴克曼。

sentences.en: And his very unusual life prepared him perfectly to tackle what might be the hardest part of a very hard job.
sentences.zh: 他非常不寻常的人生经历让他做好了充分的准备，去处理这份艰苦工作中可能最困难的部分。

sentences.en: In 1968, Rob Buckman was on stage in London's West End, doing a striptease.
sentences.zh: 1968年，罗伯·巴克曼在伦敦西区的舞台上表演脱衣舞。

sentences.en: I think the essence of it is that it was a strip routine that you might have expected a female burlesque dancer to come out and do.
sentences.zh: 我认为其精髓在于，那是一段你可能期望女性滑稽舞者出来表演的脱衣舞。

sentences.en: With Robert in this extraordinarily physically unlikely guise, going through all sorts of gestures.
sentences.zh: 罗伯以这种在身体上极其不协调的装扮，做着各种各样的动作。

sentences.en: Getting his head stuck in his pullover.
sentences.zh: 把头卡在套头衫里。

sentences.en: I mean, it wasn't all graceful, was it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这并不优雅，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, no, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不，一点也不。

sentences.en: This is Pete Atkin and Russell Davies, two of Rob's best friends.
sentences.zh: 这是皮特·阿特金和罗素·戴维斯，罗伯最好的两个朋友。

sentences.en: They were all students together at Cambridge University.
sentences.zh: 他们都是剑桥大学的同学。

sentences.en: And they were all members of the Footlights, a theatrical club.
sentences.zh: 他们都是“脚灯”剧团的成员。

sentences.en: It was a big deal to be in the Footlights then, and it still is today.
sentences.zh: 在当时，能进入“脚灯”剧团是一件了不起的事，现在依然如此。

sentences.en: The group has churned out tons of famous comedians, like half the comedy troupe Monty Python,
sentences.zh: 该团体培养了无数著名的喜剧演员，比如“蒙提·派森”喜剧团的一半成员，

sentences.en: and more recently, people like John Oliver.
sentences.zh: 以及最近的像约翰·奥利弗这样的人。

sentences.en: The Footlights put on reviews each year that featured comedy and music.
sentences.zh: “脚灯”剧团每年都会举办以喜剧和音乐为特色的演出。

sentences.en: And back in the late 60s, Rob's strip routine was a highlight.
sentences.zh: 而在60年代末，罗伯的脱衣舞表演是一个亮点。

sentences.en: He did take it absolutely seriously.
sentences.zh: 他确实非常认真地对待它。

sentences.en: He came out and did it as if people were meant to be aroused by this routine.
sentences.zh: 他走出来表演，就好像人们真的会被这段表演所挑逗一样。

sentences.en: He made great play with removing his watch, as if this were especially erotic, although there was absolutely nothing except taking off your watch like we all do.
sentences.zh: 他把摘手表的过程演得非常夸张，仿佛这特别色情，尽管这和我们平时摘手表没有任何区别。

sentences.en: There was no real punchline to it, was there, except that he had a flower painted on his stomach.
sentences.zh: 这并没有真正的笑点，对吧，除了他的肚子上画了一朵花。

sentences.en: And that was rather, rather sweet.
sentences.zh: 那倒是相当、相当可爱。

sentences.en: Rob had gone to Cambridge with the intention of becoming a doctor.
sentences.zh: 罗伯去剑桥时，本打算成为一名医生。

sentences.en: By day, he studied medicine and took classes in biochemistry.
sentences.zh: 白天，他学习医学并上生物化学课。

sentences.en: By night, he wrote and performed sketches in the Footlights club room, housed in the second story of a local fish shop.
sentences.zh: 晚上，他在位于当地一家鱼店二楼的“脚灯”俱乐部房间里编写并表演短剧。

sentences.en: He slept only three or four hours a night.
sentences.zh: 他每晚只睡三四个小时。

sentences.en: After Cambridge, Rob went to a teaching hospital.
sentences.zh: 剑桥毕业后，罗伯去了一家教学医院。

sentences.en: And it turns out that he entered medicine just as a big shift in medical culture was happening.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他进入医学界时，医学文化正发生重大转变。

sentences.en: One that changed the way doctors thought about their patients.
sentences.zh: 这种转变改变了医生对病人的看法。

sentences.en: Around the same time Rob was on stage in London's West End doing a strip routine,
sentences.zh: 就在罗伯在伦敦西区舞台上表演脱衣舞的同时，

sentences.en: a psychiatrist named Dr. Elizabeth Kubler-Ross was working on a pretty radical project.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫伊丽莎白·库伯勒-罗斯的精神科医生正在进行一个相当激进的项目。

sentences.en: She was spending time with dying patients at a hospital in Chicago, listening to their stories.
sentences.zh: 她花时间在芝加哥的一家医院陪伴垂死的病人，倾听他们的故事。

sentences.en: I just sat and listened to dying patients and tried to be their spokesman.
sentences.zh: 我只是坐着倾听垂死的病人，并试图成为他们的代言人。

sentences.en: If you can only sit and listen and hear what they say,
sentences.zh: 如果你能只是坐下来倾听并听到他们所说的话，

sentences.en: they teach you not only about dying, but about living.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅会教你关于死亡的知识，还会教你关于生活的知识。

sentences.en: In 1969, Kubler-Ross published a book based on her research called On Death and Dying.
sentences.zh: 1969年，库伯勒-罗斯根据她的研究出版了一本书，名为《论死亡与临终》。

sentences.en: You know the five stages of grief?
sentences.zh: 你知道悲伤的五个阶段吗？

sentences.en: That's where that comes from.
sentences.zh: 那就是从那里来的。

sentences.en: The book became an international bestseller and brought conversations about dying into the home.
sentences.zh: 这本书成为了国际畅销书，并将关于死亡的对话带入了家庭。

sentences.en: Kubler-Ross also encouraged doctors to speak more frankly with their patients about death.
sentences.zh: 库伯勒-罗斯还鼓励医生更坦率地与病人谈论死亡。

sentences.en: She said they needed to stop tiptoeing around the subject.
sentences.zh: 她说他们需要停止在这个话题上小心翼翼。

sentences.en: Which is what doctors had done for most of the history of modern medicine.
sentences.zh: 而这正是医生在现代医学史上大部分时间里所做的事情。

sentences.en: The original code of ethics established by the American Medical Association in 1847 said
sentences.zh: 美国医学会在1847年制定的最初道德准则称，

sentences.en: it wasn't the role of doctors to make, quote, gloomy prognostications, unquote.
sentences.zh: 医生的职责不是做出所谓的“悲观预测”。

sentences.en: Instead, they should be ministers of hope and comfort.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们应该是希望和安慰的使者。

sentences.en: Doctors were afraid that disclosing a bad diagnosis would actually be damaging
sentences.zh: 医生们担心披露糟糕的诊断结果实际上会造成伤害，

sentences.en: and could even drive patients to suicide.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能导致病人自杀。

sentences.en: This attitude remained unchanged through much of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这种态度在20世纪的大部分时间里都没有改变。

sentences.en: In the 50s, the word cancer wasn't used.
sentences.zh: 在50年代，人们不使用“癌症”这个词。

sentences.en: Dr. Walter Bale is a psychiatrist and a professor at the MD Anderson Cancer Center.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特·贝尔医生是一位精神科医生，也是MD安德森癌症中心的教授。

sentences.en: It's part of the University of Texas in Houston.
sentences.zh: 它是休斯顿德克萨斯大学的一部分。

sentences.en: There was a lot of deception that went on around how sick people really were.
sentences.zh: 在病人到底病得有多重的问题上，存在着大量的欺骗。

sentences.en: You couldn't talk about the patient dying.
sentences.zh: 你不能谈论病人即将死亡。

sentences.en: So you can imagine nobody really was able to say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象，没有人能真正做到告别。

sentences.en: In 1951, the Journal of the American Medical Association actually published methods for
sentences.zh: 1951年，《美国医学会杂志》甚至发表了关于

sentences.en: deceiving cancer patients and their families.
sentences.zh: 欺骗癌症患者及其家属的方法。

sentences.en: They recommended giving evasive answers or using confusing euphemisms,
sentences.zh: 他们建议给出含糊其辞的回答或使用令人困惑的委婉语，

sentences.en: like calling cancer an ulcer or an infection.
sentences.zh: 比如把癌症称为溃疡或感染。

sentences.en: The same article recommended that cancer patients who learned the truth of their diagnosis
sentences.zh: 同一篇文章建议，对于得知诊断真相并反应强烈的癌症患者，

sentences.en: and reacted badly to it be given lobotomies.
sentences.zh: 可以对他们进行脑叶切除术。

sentences.en: And this attitude was pervasive.
sentences.zh: 这种态度非常普遍。

sentences.en: In 1961, a survey showed that 90% of doctors preferred not to disclose cancer diagnoses to patients,
sentences.zh: 1961年的一项调查显示，90%的医生倾向于不向病人披露癌症诊断结果，

sentences.en: despite another study showing that the vast majority of patients wanted to know the truth.
sentences.zh: 尽管另一项研究表明，绝大多数病人希望知道真相。

sentences.en: But then things started to change.
sentences.zh: 但随后情况开始发生变化。

sentences.en: In the 1960s, doctors developed effective treatments for cancer.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪60年代，医生开发出了有效的癌症治疗方法。

sentences.en: The two big advancements were chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
sentences.zh: 两大进步是化学疗法和放射疗法。

sentences.en: The research just exploded.
sentences.zh: 研究成果呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: Patients have a lot more to hope for than they did in the 50s.
sentences.zh: 病人比50年代有了更多的希望。

sentences.en: And around the same time, palliative care emerged as a concept in medicine.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，姑息治疗作为一个医学概念出现了。

sentences.en: We began to realize that controlling pain and other symptoms could give people a peaceful death.
sentences.zh: 我们开始意识到，控制疼痛和其他症状可以让人平静地离世。

sentences.en: The modern palliative care movement, together with hospice, has really made death less fearful for people.
sentences.zh: 现代姑息治疗运动，连同临终关怀，确实让人们对死亡不再那么恐惧。

sentences.en: These developments, along with the work of Elizabeth Kupala-Ross,
sentences.zh: 这些发展，加上伊丽莎白·库伯勒-罗斯的工作，

sentences.en: all started to change the way our culture talked about death and dying.
sentences.zh: 都开始改变我们文化中谈论死亡和临终的方式。

sentences.en: And it was in this context that Rob Buckman became a doctor.
sentences.zh: 正是在这种背景下，罗伯·巴克曼成为了一名医生。

sentences.en: A doctor whose totally irreverent take on medicine would ultimately help him transform the field.
sentences.zh: 一位对医学持完全不敬态度的医生，他最终帮助改变了这个领域。

sentences.en: Rob's work in the Cambridge Footlights got him noticed by the BBC.
sentences.zh: 罗布在剑桥脚灯剧社的工作让他受到了BBC的关注。

sentences.en: While still training as a doctor, he wrote and performed on radio and TV.
sentences.zh: 在接受医生培训的同时，他还在广播和电视上进行创作和表演。

sentences.en: In 1978, he and his writing partner were given their own comedy program.
sentences.zh: 1978年，他和他的创作搭档拥有了自己的喜剧节目。

sentences.en: It was called The Pink Medicine Show.
sentences.zh: 节目名叫《粉红医药秀》。

sentences.en: The Pink Medicine Show was like SNL or MADtv, but all medical sketches.
sentences.zh: 《粉红医药秀》就像《周六夜现场》或《MADtv》，但全是关于医疗的短剧。

sentences.en: There was actually a lot of comedy about medicine at this time, especially in Britain.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当时有很多关于医学的喜剧，尤其是在英国。

sentences.en: Doctors were seen as these stodgy and distant authority figures, so they made a good target for satire.
sentences.zh: 医生们被视为那种古板且高高在上的权威人物，所以他们成了讽刺的好目标。

sentences.en: One of Rob's recurring characters on the show was a malingerer, a guy pretending to be sick,
sentences.zh: 罗布在节目中有一个常驻角色，是个装病的人，一个假装生病的人，

sentences.en: who keeps showing up at the hospital with different ridiculous excuses.
sentences.zh: 他总是带着各种荒谬的借口出现在医院里。

sentences.en: What is it?
sentences.zh: 怎么了？

sentences.en: It's about my bowels.
sentences.zh: 是关于我的肠道问题。

sentences.en: Your bowels?
sentences.zh: 你的肠道？

sentences.en: I mean, what's the matter?
sentences.zh: 我是说，到底哪里不舒服？

sentences.en: Aren't they regular or something?
sentences.zh: 是不规律还是怎么着？

sentences.en: Oh no, no, I am regular.
sentences.zh: 哦不，不，我很规律。

sentences.en: Every morning on the dot of eight o'clock.
sentences.zh: 每天早上八点整。

sentences.en: Every morning on the dot of eight o'clock?
sentences.zh: 每天早上八点整？

sentences.en: I mean, that's marvellous.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那太棒了。

sentences.en: What are you worried about?
sentences.zh: 那你担心什么呢？

sentences.en: I don't wake up till nine.
sentences.zh: 我九点才醒。

sentences.en: Rob's success caught the attention of another Footlights alum.
sentences.zh: 罗布的成功引起了另一位脚灯剧社校友的注意。

sentences.en: Mostly we laughed a lot because he was funny.
sentences.zh: 我们大多时候都在大笑，因为他很有趣。

sentences.en: He was one of the half-dozen people that I spent most of my time laughing with.
sentences.zh: 他是我花最多时间一起欢笑的那六七个人之一。

sentences.en: That's John Cleese.
sentences.zh: 那就是约翰·克里斯。

sentences.en: You know, Monty Python, Fawlty Towers, A Fish Called Wanda, the James Bond movies.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，《蒙提·派森》、《弗尔蒂旅馆》、《一条叫旺达的鱼》，还有詹姆斯·邦德系列电影。

sentences.en: I think he's in one of the Harry Potters.
sentences.zh: 我想他还在其中一部《哈利·波特》里演过。

sentences.en: Anyway, when I reached him, he was getting ready to go on safari.
sentences.zh: 总之，当我联系上他时，他正准备去参加游猎旅行。

sentences.en: Well, I'm off tomorrow for three and a half months, so I'm in the usual state of wondering what I've forgotten to pack.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我明天就要出发去三个半月，所以我正处于那种惯常的状态，在想自己忘了带什么。

sentences.en: In 1979, John Cleese was producing The Secret Policeman's Ball, a comedy show that benefited Amnesty International.
sentences.zh: 1979年，约翰·克里斯正在制作《秘密警察舞会》，这是一场为国际特赦组织筹款的喜剧演出。

sentences.en: And he asked Rob if he'd appear in a sketch with him and Michael Palin, the old Monty Python bit known as the Cheese Shop Sketch.
sentences.zh: 他邀请罗布和他以及迈克尔·佩林一起表演一个短剧，就是那个著名的《奶酪店》短剧。

sentences.en: Now then, my good man, some cheese, if you please.
sentences.zh: 那么，这位好先生，请给我来点奶酪。

sentences.en: Oh, yes, sir, yes, sir.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的，先生，好的，先生。

sentences.en: What would you like?
sentences.zh: 您想要点什么？

sentences.en: Uh, how about a little red Leicester?
sentences.zh: 呃，来点莱斯特红奶酪怎么样？

sentences.en: I'm afraid we're fresher, a red Leicester.
sentences.zh: 恐怕我们没有新鲜的莱斯特红奶酪了。

sentences.en: Um, yes, it's a very silly Python sketch in which a man goes into a cheese shop to buy some cheese
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这是一个非常滑稽的派森短剧，讲的是一个人走进一家奶酪店想买奶酪，

sentences.en: and it slowly becomes obvious that they don't actually have any, any cheese in the shop.
sentences.zh: 结果慢慢发现店里其实根本没有任何奶酪。

sentences.en: Torwinzo?
sentences.zh: 托温佐奶酪？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Parmesan?
sentences.zh: 帕尔马干酪？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Mozzarella?
sentences.zh: 马苏里拉奶酪？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Tupo creme?
sentences.zh: 图波奶油奶酪？

sentences.en: As the man puts it, it seems to be a shop entirely uncontaminated by cheese.
sentences.zh: 正如那个人所说，这似乎是一家完全没被奶酪污染的店。

sentences.en: Venezuelan beaver cheese, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 也许有委内瑞拉海狸奶酪？

sentences.en: LAUGHTER
sentences.zh: 笑声

sentences.en: They're not today, sir.
sentences.zh: 今天没有，先生。

sentences.en: The whole time this ridiculous exchange is taking place, a Greek bouzouki band is playing in the background of the shop
sentences.zh: 就在这段荒谬的对话进行时，店里的背景里正播放着希腊布祖基琴音乐，

sentences.en: and there are two guys doing a weird dance with their arms around each other's shoulders.
sentences.zh: 还有两个家伙搂着肩膀跳着奇怪的舞蹈。

sentences.en: One of those guys was Rob.
sentences.zh: 其中一个家伙就是罗布。

sentences.en: And then at a certain point, my character got so irritated by the lack of cheese
sentences.zh: 然后在某个时刻，我的角色因为没有奶酪而变得非常恼火，

sentences.en: that I turned and snapped at the Greek dancers.
sentences.zh: 以至于我转过身去对那些希腊舞者发火。

sentences.en: Will you stop it?
sentences.zh: 你们能停下吗？

sentences.en: Who then stopped and slunk off.
sentences.zh: 他们随后停下来溜走了。

sentences.en: Rob's appearance with Monty Python marked one of the high points of his comedy career.
sentences.zh: 罗布与《蒙提·派森》的合作标志着他喜剧生涯的高光时刻之一。

sentences.en: But if you look closely, you might notice his face looks pale and a little puffy.
sentences.zh: 但如果你仔细看，可能会发现他的脸色苍白，还有点浮肿。

sentences.en: That's because after finishing his medical training and establishing himself in the comedy world,
sentences.zh: 那是因为在完成医学培训并确立了自己在喜剧界的地位后，

sentences.en: Rob got really, really sick.
sentences.zh: 罗布病得非常非常重。

sentences.en: Soon, Rob would learn firsthand what it was like to be a dying patient.
sentences.zh: 很快，罗布将亲身体验到作为一个垂死病人的感受。

sentences.en: And this role reversal, from doctor to sick person, would transform how he thought about his work as a physician
sentences.zh: 这种从医生到病人的角色转换，将改变他对自己作为医生的工作的看法，

sentences.en: and the process of breaking bad news.
sentences.zh: 以及他处理告知坏消息这一过程的方式。

sentences.en: In April 1978, I contracted a very interesting and fairly rare disease.
sentences.zh: 1978年4月，我得了一种非常有趣且相当罕见的疾病。

sentences.en: Interesting not just because it affected me and turned me from a doctor into a patient,
sentences.zh: 之所以有趣，不仅因为它影响了我，让我从医生变成了病人，

sentences.en: but also because it's one of a group of diseases in which the body's defenses attack the body itself
sentences.zh: 还因为它属于那种身体防御系统攻击自身的一类疾病，

sentences.en: and in which you become literally your own worst enemy.
sentences.zh: 在那种情况下，你真的成了自己最大的敌人。

sentences.en: That's Rob from a TV documentary he made about his illness as he was becoming sicker.
sentences.zh: 那是罗布在他病情加重时为自己拍摄的一部电视纪录片里的片段。

sentences.en: It's called Your Own Worst Enemy.
sentences.zh: 片名叫《你最大的敌人》。

sentences.en: It began very simply and very mildly with pain in my right wriSt.
sentences.zh: 它开始得非常简单且轻微，只是右手腕疼痛。

sentences.en: And when I moved my wrist, it creaked.
sentences.zh: 当我活动手腕时，它会发出咯吱声。

sentences.en: And at that point...
sentences.zh: 就在那时……

sentences.en: Rob had dermatomyositis, a very rare autoimmune disease.
sentences.zh: 罗布患的是皮肌炎，一种非常罕见的自身免疫性疾病。

sentences.en: The disease causes your body to malfunction and attack its own muscle tissue.
sentences.zh: 这种病会导致身体机能失调，攻击自身的肌肉组织。

sentences.en: So Rob wasted away.
sentences.zh: 所以罗布日渐消瘦。

sentences.en: And he developed these rashes all over his body.
sentences.zh: 他的全身还长出了这些皮疹。

sentences.en: At one point, I couldn't actually put my hands behind my head because so much of the skin was inflamed.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我甚至无法把手放到脑后，因为大部分皮肤都发炎了。

sentences.en: It was like wearing a leather jacket that had been shrunken onto you or was sort of encased in it.
sentences.zh: 就像穿了一件缩水在身上的皮夹克，或者被它包裹住了一样。

sentences.en: Rob was married at this point and had two daughters.
sentences.zh: 罗布当时已经结婚，有两个女儿。

sentences.en: One of the more poignant moments of the film captures Rob trying and failing to pick up one of his girls.
sentences.zh: 影片中最感人的时刻之一，捕捉到了罗布试图抱起其中一个女儿却失败的场景。

sentences.en: He talks about how weak and vulnerable he feels.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了自己感到多么虚弱和脆弱。

sentences.en: What happens is very, very simply, the color drains out of everything.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情非常非常简单，一切事物的色彩都褪去了。

sentences.en: It's the same scene.
sentences.zh: 还是同样的场景。

sentences.en: It's the same family.
sentences.zh: 还是同样的家庭。

sentences.en: It's the same house.
sentences.zh: 还是同样的房子。

sentences.en: But all the color, the things you enjoy, have simply the tone of the illness about them.
sentences.zh: 但所有的色彩，那些你曾经享受的事物，都染上了疾病的色调。

sentences.en: For a while, Rob's condition was so bad that his doctors thought he might not make it.
sentences.zh: 有一段时间，罗布的病情非常严重，医生们以为他挺不过去了。

sentences.en: And the experience of being that close to death was profound.
sentences.zh: 那种濒临死亡的经历是非常深刻的。

sentences.en: Years later, he'd recall an especially important encounter with one of his physicians.
sentences.zh: 多年后，他回忆起与其中一位医生的一次特别重要的会面。

sentences.en: And I was sitting there and I was very arthritic and I had all kinds of problems with the skin and bowel and everything.
sentences.zh: 我坐在那里，患有严重的关节炎，皮肤、肠道等等都有各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: I was in deep trouble.
sentences.zh: 我陷入了深重的困境。

sentences.en: And I was feeling lousy.
sentences.zh: 我感觉糟透了。

sentences.en: He said, you've got this, you've got that, you've got the other, you've got the skin, you've got the muscles.
sentences.zh: 他说，你有这个，你有那个，你有其他的问题，你的皮肤，你的肌肉。

sentences.en: It must be awful for you.
sentences.zh: 这对你来说一定很糟糕。

sentences.en: I am sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: It must be awful for you.
sentences.zh: 这对你来说一定很糟糕。

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 我很抱歉。

sentences.en: And I very nearly burst into tears and hugged him because he gave me permission to feel ill.
sentences.zh: 我差点就泪流满面并拥抱了他，因为他给了我感到痛苦的许可。

sentences.en: The doctor was telling Rob that it was okay to have feelings about being sick, that the negative emotions were a valid part of the experience.
sentences.zh: 医生是在告诉罗布，对生病有情绪是正常的，负面情绪是这种经历中合理的一部分。

sentences.en: The doctor was paying attention not just to Rob's physical state, but also his emotional state.
sentences.zh: 医生不仅关注罗布的身体状况，还关注他的情绪状态。

sentences.en: And while this might seem obvious, it wasn't especially common for doctors to do this back then.
sentences.zh: 虽然这看起来很显而易见，但在当时，医生这样做并不常见。

sentences.en: This moment was simple but important.
sentences.zh: 这一刻虽然简单，却很重要。

sentences.en: It would go on to become the cornerstone of Rob's approach to doctor-patient communication.
sentences.zh: 它后来成为了罗布医患沟通方法论的基石。

sentences.en: And then, little by little, Rob started getting better.
sentences.zh: 然后，一点一点地，罗布开始好转。

sentences.en: He was having blood plasma replacement therapy and a new drug he was taking started to work.
sentences.zh: 他接受了血浆置换疗法，并且他服用的一种新药开始起效了。

sentences.en: The last four weeks have been like a gift.
sentences.zh: 过去四周就像是一份礼物。

sentences.en: I can drive my car, I can straighten my elbows, I can dress myself, I can put any kind of socks on, even woolly socks.
sentences.zh: 我可以开车，可以伸直手肘，可以自己穿衣，可以穿上任何袜子，甚至是羊毛袜。

sentences.en: By May of 1980, Rob's condition had turned around.
sentences.zh: 到1980年5月，罗布的病情已经好转。

sentences.en: I can go for walks in the park with the kids and not feel too bad about it.
sentences.zh: 我可以带孩子们去公园散步，也不会觉得太难受。

sentences.en: And I can stay awake all day and watch television in the evening or whatever,
sentences.zh: 我可以整天保持清醒，晚上看电视什么的，

sentences.en: and I can go to bed at midnight and live a normal life, which is really, is fabulous.
sentences.zh: 我可以在午夜上床睡觉，过上正常的生活，这真是太棒了。

sentences.en: For Rob, normal life meant going back to his incredibly intense work schedule.
sentences.zh: 对罗布来说，正常生活意味着回到他那极其繁重的工作日程中。

sentences.en: He was more successful than ever, training as a specialist in oncology, which is the branch of medicine that deals with cancer,
sentences.zh: 他比以往任何时候都更成功，他正在接受肿瘤学专家的培训，这是医学中处理癌症的分支，

sentences.en: while simultaneously co-hosting a popular TV science show called Where There's Life.
sentences.zh: 同时还共同主持一档名为《生命所在之处》的流行电视科学节目。

sentences.en: Where There's Life returns as doctors Miriam Stoppard and Rob Buckman explore such topics as cosmetic surgery, unwed mothers, and the nursing profession.
sentences.zh: 《生命所在之处》回归了，医生米里亚姆·斯托帕德和罗布·巴克曼将探讨整容手术、未婚母亲和护理行业等话题。

sentences.en: But that intensity wasn't good for his marriage.
sentences.zh: 但那种高强度的工作对他的婚姻并不好。

sentences.en: He and his wife ended up getting a divorce, and in 1985, Rob moved to Toronto to take a job at a hospital.
sentences.zh: 他和妻子最终离婚了，1985年，罗布搬到多伦多，在一家医院找到了一份工作。

sentences.en: In Canada, Rob had to restart his life completely, but it was there he would end up making his most lasting contributions to the field of medicine.
sentences.zh: 在加拿大，罗布不得不彻底重启人生，但正是在那里，他最终为医学界做出了最持久的贡献。

sentences.en: He started studying the way that doctors communicated with people they were treating.
sentences.zh: 他开始研究医生与患者沟通的方式。

sentences.en: Specifically, he was interested in how doctors interacted with dying patients, because he himself had recently been a dying patient.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，他感兴趣的是医生如何与垂死的病人互动，因为他自己最近也曾是一名垂死的病人。

sentences.en: This is from an interview he gave in 1999.
sentences.zh: 这是他1999年接受采访时说的话。

sentences.en: The great thing about being ill from my point of view was that I found out that I could tolerate,
sentences.zh: 从我的角度来看，生病的好处在于我发现我能够忍受，

sentences.en: I mean, I did tolerate a fair amount of pain and handicap and so on, but I didn't collapse.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我确实忍受了相当多的痛苦和残疾等等，但我没有崩溃。

sentences.en: I wasn't a hero by any means, but I wasn't a different person.
sentences.zh: 我绝不是什么英雄，但我也没有变成另一个人。

sentences.en: His big realization was that doctors didn't need to hide information from their patients and tiptoe through tough subjects.
sentences.zh: 他最大的感悟是，医生不需要对病人隐瞒信息，也不需要对棘手的话题小心翼翼。

sentences.en: Sick people could withstand a lot.
sentences.zh: 病人是可以承受很多东西的。

sentences.en: So when I recovered, I was then able to say, okay, I've been under fire, and I stayed the same.
sentences.zh: 所以当我康复后，我就能说，好吧，我经历过战火，但我依然是我。

sentences.en: Now I can be brave when talking to the patient.
sentences.zh: 现在我可以勇敢地与病人交谈了。

sentences.en: He walked in my room like a breath of not fresh air.
sentences.zh: 他走进我的房间，就像一阵……不是新鲜空气。

sentences.en: It was sort of like a wind, this huge energy sort of exploding into the room,
sentences.zh: 那更像是一阵风，巨大的能量在房间里爆发开来，

sentences.en: and I'd never actually met anybody quite like him before.
sentences.zh: 我以前从未见过像他这样的人。

sentences.en: I think most people haven't.
sentences.zh: 我想大多数人都没有见过。

sentences.en: Dr. Patricia Shaw was a cancer researcher at the same hospital where Rob worked in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 帕特里夏·肖医生是罗布在多伦多工作的那家医院的癌症研究员。

sentences.en: She goes by Pat.
sentences.zh: 她叫帕特。

sentences.en: Pat and Rob met in the most Dr. Lee meet-cute scenario imaginable.
sentences.zh: 帕特和罗布的相遇是你能想象到的最典型的医生式浪漫邂逅。

sentences.en: He was told that I had the best microscope.
sentences.zh: 有人告诉他我有最好的显微镜。

sentences.en: I had the newest microscope.
sentences.zh: 我有最新的显微镜。

sentences.en: And so he came in to see me.
sentences.zh: 所以他来看我。

sentences.en: And that's how we really met our first conversation.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们真正相遇的第一次谈话。

sentences.en: One thing led to another, and they got married in 1988.
sentences.zh: 后来顺理成章，他们在1988年结婚了。

sentences.en: It was around this time that Rob started writing more.
sentences.zh: 大约就在这个时候，罗布开始更多地进行写作。

sentences.en: He had a large piece of solid mahogany that he'd brought with him from England.
sentences.zh: 他有一大块从英国带来的实心红木板。

sentences.en: And his favorite spot was to sit at this desk at his computer.
sentences.zh: 他最喜欢的地方就是坐在书桌前的电脑旁。

sentences.en: So even though he was really busy at the hospital, he spent a huge amount of time after those hours working in his study.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管他在医院非常忙，但他还是花大量时间在下班后待在书房里工作。

sentences.en: Rob wrote a book called I Don't Know What to Say, How to Help and Support Someone Who is Dying.
sentences.zh: 罗布写了一本书，叫《我不知道该说什么：如何帮助和支持垂死之人》。

sentences.en: It's kind of like what to expect when you're expecting.
sentences.zh: 这有点像《孕期完全指南》那样的书。

sentences.en: If what you're expecting is that somebody close to you is going to die soon.
sentences.zh: 如果你的预期是你的亲近之人即将离世。

sentences.en: It's a very frank but easy-to-read book that covers everything from basic listening skills to the sexual needs of the dying to survivor's guilt.
sentences.zh: 这是一本非常坦率但易读的书，涵盖了从基本的倾听技巧到垂死之人的性需求，再到幸存者内疚感等方方面面。

sentences.en: And then in 1992, Rob published the most important book of his career.
sentences.zh: 然后在1992年，罗布出版了他职业生涯中最重要的书。

sentences.en: It was titled How to Break Bad News, the first medical textbook on the subject.
sentences.zh: 书名是《如何告知坏消息》，这是该领域的第一本医学教科书。

sentences.en: When Rob Buckman wrote the book on how to give bad news, it was from his experience as an oncologist having to give it several times a week.
sentences.zh: 当罗布·巴克曼写下关于如何告知坏消息的书时，那是基于他作为一名肿瘤科医生，每周都要多次告知坏消息的经验。

sentences.en: That's Dr. Walter Bale again.
sentences.zh: 那又是沃尔特·贝尔医生。

sentences.en: He was also studying doctor-patient communication when Rob's book came out.
sentences.zh: 罗伯的书出版时，他也在研究医患沟通。

sentences.en: He understood that bad news was a series of steps.
sentences.zh: 他明白告知坏消息是一个循序渐进的过程。

sentences.en: It could be broken down into a series of steps.
sentences.zh: 它可以被拆解为一系列步骤。

sentences.en: Walter and Rob would eventually write a set of guidelines based on Rob's book.
sentences.zh: 沃尔特和罗伯最终根据罗伯的书编写了一套指导方针。

sentences.en: They called their strategy the SPIKES protocol.
sentences.zh: 他们将这套策略称为SPIKES方案。

sentences.en: SPIKES was an acronym that stood for setting, perception, invitation, knowledge, emotions, strategy and summary.
sentences.zh: SPIKES是一个首字母缩略词，代表环境（Setting）、感知（Perception）、邀请（Invitation）、知识（Knowledge）、情绪（Emotions）、策略与总结（Strategy and Summary）。

sentences.en: It's a mnemonic device that doctors can use as they prepare to give bad news and then during the actual conversation with the patient so that it doesn't fly off the rails.
sentences.zh: 这是一种记忆辅助工具，医生在准备告知坏消息时，以及在与患者进行实际交谈时都可以使用，以防谈话失控。

sentences.en: You didn't worry that it sounded too, I don't know, spiky?
sentences.zh: 你不担心这听起来太……我不知道，太尖锐（spiky）了吗？

sentences.en: No, we didn't even think about it because it was so elegant.
sentences.zh: 不，我们甚至没想过这个问题，因为它太精妙了。

sentences.en: Everybody remembers that.
sentences.zh: 每个人都记得这个词。

sentences.en: Soon, Walter and Rob were giving presentations on spikes at hospitals all over the world.
sentences.zh: 很快，沃尔特和罗伯就开始在世界各地的医院里做关于SPIKES的演讲。

sentences.en: They made videos for medical schools which demonstrated how spikes could help doctors navigate these difficult conversations.
sentences.zh: 他们为医学院制作了视频，演示了SPIKES如何帮助医生处理这些艰难的对话。

sentences.en: In some of the videos, Rob performs improvised scenes with actors playing patients or family members, just like you heard Artie doing with Mark at the beginning of this episode.
sentences.zh: 在一些视频中，罗伯与扮演患者或家属的演员进行即兴表演，就像你在这集开头听到阿蒂和马克做的那样。

sentences.en: Not real, but really intense.
sentences.zh: 虽然不是真的，但非常真实且强烈。

sentences.en: Here is the six-step protocol, which has the rather inelegant and threatening acronym SPIKES.
sentences.zh: 这就是这套六步方案，它有着一个相当不优雅且带有威胁意味的首字母缩略词：SPIKES。

sentences.en: The letters stand for S for setting.
sentences.zh: 字母S代表环境（Setting）。

sentences.en: Getting the physical context right.
sentences.zh: 营造合适的物理环境。

sentences.en: Sit down.
sentences.zh: 坐下来。

sentences.en: Try to look relaxed.
sentences.zh: 尽量看起来放松。

sentences.en: Make eye contact.
sentences.zh: 保持眼神交流。

sentences.en: Accept if the patient is either angry or crying.
sentences.zh: 如果患者生气或哭泣，要予以接纳。

sentences.en: Important to have Kleenex right at hand.
sentences.zh: 手边准备好纸巾很重要。

sentences.en: Perception.
sentences.zh: 感知（Perception）。

sentences.en: Assessing the patient's perception of his or her medical situation.
sentences.zh: 评估患者对自己医疗状况的认知。

sentences.en: When you got that chest pain or when you found that lump in your breast, what did you think was going on?
sentences.zh: 当你感到胸痛或者发现乳房有肿块时，你觉得是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Then comes the pivot of the whole interview, when you ask the patient what he or she would like to know.
sentences.zh: 接下来是整个谈话的关键转折点，询问患者想了解多少信息。

sentences.en: Hence, eye for invitation.
sentences.zh: 因此，I代表邀请（Invitation）。

sentences.en: Do you want to know the exact results of the bone scan and know what is going on?
sentences.zh: 你想知道骨扫描的确切结果并了解具体情况吗？

sentences.en: Is that the kind of way you'd like me to handle the information?
sentences.zh: 你希望我以这种方式向你告知信息吗？

sentences.en: Yes, please.
sentences.zh: 是的，请告知。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: K for knowledge.
sentences.zh: K代表知识（Knowledge）。

sentences.en: Giving the medical facts.
sentences.zh: 提供医学事实。

sentences.en: Dr. Wilson took a little bit of that growth from the lung and we looked at it under the microscope.
sentences.zh: 威尔逊医生从肺部取了一点增生物，我们在显微镜下观察了它。

sentences.en: I'll go ahead and tell you what it was.
sentences.zh: 我现在就告诉你结果。

sentences.en: Give the information in small chunks and always check that the patient understands what you are saying after each small chunk.
sentences.zh: 分小块提供信息，并在每一小块之后确认患者是否理解。

sentences.en: It showed that the growth was a malignant growth, a cancer, in other words, of the lung.
sentences.zh: 结果显示该增生物是恶性的，换句话说，是肺癌。

sentences.en: I have cancer of my lung.
sentences.zh: 我得了肺癌。

sentences.en: And the all-important E for emotions.
sentences.zh: 以及至关重要的E，代表情绪（Emotions）。

sentences.en: Acknowledge and name the emotion that the patient is expressing.
sentences.zh: 确认并点出患者表达的情绪。

sentences.en: This is obviously a great shock to you.
sentences.zh: 这对你来说显然是一个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: This is difficult to believe.
sentences.zh: 这让人难以置信。

sentences.en: This must make you feel awful.
sentences.zh: 这一定让你感觉很糟糕。

sentences.en: This is overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 这让人难以承受。

sentences.en: Your ability to empathize with the patient's emotions is the single most important characteristic of good and supportive newsbreaking.
sentences.zh: 你与患者情绪共情的能力，是良好且具支持性的坏消息告知过程中最重要的特质。

sentences.en: Without it, you're going to appear insensitive and of little support.
sentences.zh: 没有它，你会显得麻木不仁，无法提供多少支持。

sentences.en: And then S, strategy and summary.
sentences.zh: 最后是S，策略与总结（Strategy and Summary）。

sentences.en: So what do we do from here?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来我们该怎么办？

sentences.en: What we do from here is very important.
sentences.zh: 接下来我们要做的非常重要。

sentences.en: Whatever it is that's going to happen next, make it clear.
sentences.zh: 无论接下来会发生什么，都要表达清楚。

sentences.en: As you can hear from those scenes, Rob was masterful at breaking bad news.
sentences.zh: 正如你从那些场景中听到的，罗伯在告知坏消息方面非常精通。

sentences.en: He was calm, present, compassionate, and clear.
sentences.zh: 他冷静、专注、富有同情心且表达清晰。

sentences.en: And he was good at it not just because he'd been a patient, but because he'd been a comedian.
sentences.zh: 他之所以擅长这一点，不仅因为他曾是一名患者，还因为他曾是一名喜剧演员。

sentences.en: It's the ability to put yourself in your audience's shoes and understand what makes them tick, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一种能够设身处地为观众着想，并理解他们关注点的能力，对吧？

sentences.en: So if you're a comedian, you want to know what you can do to make people laugh, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是喜剧演员，你会想知道怎么做才能让人发笑，对吧？

sentences.en: If you're a doctor, you need to put yourself in people's shoes and imagine what they need in order to make sense out of the process of giving bad news.
sentences.zh: 如果你是医生，你需要设身处地为他人着想，想象他们需要什么，才能理解告知坏消息的过程。

sentences.en: Even though Rob had recovered from his illness, it had taken a toll on his body and he had health problems for the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 尽管罗伯从疾病中康复了，但这对他身体造成了损害，余生他一直伴有健康问题。

sentences.en: A case of shingles left him paralyzed on one side.
sentences.zh: 一次带状疱疹让他一侧身体瘫痪。

sentences.en: He had difficulty dressing himself and walking, and he couldn't drive a car.
sentences.zh: 他穿衣和走路都很困难，也不能开车。

sentences.en: And that was pretty devastating.
sentences.zh: 那真是太令人沮丧了。

sentences.en: Again, Rob's wife, Pat.
sentences.zh: 再次提到罗伯的妻子，帕特。

sentences.en: To have this insult, leaving him with this permanent deficit, I think was really, really damaging, and he had a hard time coping with that.
sentences.zh: 遭受这样的打击，留下永久性的残疾，我认为真的非常、非常具有破坏性，他很难应对这一切。

sentences.en: But in his typical Rob way, he kept working on his many projects.
sentences.zh: 但以他典型的罗伯式风格，他继续致力于他的许多项目。

sentences.en: In 2011, he flew to London to film a series of health videos with Terry Jones, another member of Monty Python.
sentences.zh: 2011年，他飞往伦敦，与蒙提·派森的另一位成员特里·琼斯拍摄了一系列健康视频。

sentences.en: Then he got back on the plane to Toronto.
sentences.zh: 然后他坐飞机回多伦多。

sentences.en: After his flight got in, he didn't arrive and he wasn't answering his text messages.
sentences.zh: 航班抵达后，他没有出现，也没有回复短信。

sentences.en: It wasn't too unusual.
sentences.zh: 这并不太反常。

sentences.en: He traveled so much, flights got delayed.
sentences.zh: 他经常旅行，航班延误很常见。

sentences.en: I went to bed, and about midnight, there was a knock on the door and there was a policeman at the door.
sentences.zh: 我上床睡觉了，大约午夜时分，有人敲门，门外站着一名警察。

sentences.en: Doctors aren't the only ones who have to break bad news.
sentences.zh: 医生并不是唯一需要告知坏消息的人。

sentences.en: He talked a bit of nonsense and then asked if I was Mrs. Buckman, and then eventually got around to saying that Rob had passed away.
sentences.zh: 他说了些莫名其妙的话，然后问我是不是巴克曼夫人，最后终于说出罗伯已经去世了。

sentences.en: Rob had died in his sleep on the plane from an undiagnosed heart condition.
sentences.zh: 罗伯在飞机上睡梦中因未被诊断出的心脏病去世了。

sentences.en: He was only 63.
sentences.zh: 他才63岁。

sentences.en: It took Pat a long time to get over the shock.
sentences.zh: 帕特花了很长时间才从震惊中走出来。

sentences.en: There was so much about missing Rob.
sentences.zh: 有太多关于怀念罗伯的思绪。

sentences.en: There was so much about having to deal with the realities of what happens when somebody dies.
sentences.zh: 还有太多关于处理某人去世后现实问题的琐事。

sentences.en: And even though Rob himself had talked openly about death and dying,
sentences.zh: 尽管罗伯本人曾公开谈论过死亡和临终问题，

sentences.en: even though he'd spent years writing books that encouraged people to be frank about these subjects,
sentences.zh: 尽管他花了多年时间写书，鼓励人们坦诚面对这些话题，

sentences.en: he wasn't actually ready for his own death.
sentences.zh: 但他实际上并没有为自己的死亡做好准备。

sentences.en: In real terms, you know, like finance and insurance and all that kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 在现实层面，你知道，比如财务、保险之类的各种事情。

sentences.en: So it was hard.
sentences.zh: 所以这很难。

sentences.en: Even now, it's six years later, and it still makes me a bit teary thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 即使现在，六年过去了，想到这些我仍然会有点热泪盈眶。

sentences.en: Beyond Rob's death, Spikes has endured.
sentences.zh: 在罗伯去世后，SPIKES方案依然沿用至今。

sentences.en: It's been absorbed into the mainstream of American medicine.
sentences.zh: 它已被纳入美国医学的主流。

sentences.en: Just recently, the American Society of Clinical Oncology started recommending that doctors use a protocol when giving bad news.
sentences.zh: 就在最近，美国临床肿瘤学会开始建议医生在告知坏消息时使用某种方案。

sentences.en: They offer Spikes as a good example.
sentences.zh: 他们将SPIKES作为一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: And Spikes is taught in many medical schools in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 而且SPIKES在美国的许多医学院中都有教授，

sentences.en: and Canada,
sentences.zh: 在加拿大也是，

sentences.en: as well as schools in Europe, Asia, and South America.
sentences.zh: 以及欧洲、亚洲和南美洲的学校。

sentences.en: You remember Artie, the medical student from the top of the show?
sentences.zh: 还记得节目开头提到的医学生阿蒂吗？

sentences.en: He used Spikes to navigate his encounter with Mark, the actor.
sentences.zh: 他使用了SPIKES方案来处理他与演员马克的那次模拟对话。

sentences.en: Oh, gosh.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think if I hadn't had the Spikes protocol training beforehand,
sentences.zh: 是的，我想如果我之前没有接受过SPIKES方案的培训，

sentences.en: I would have been completely loSt.
sentences.zh: 我会完全不知所措。

sentences.en: I would not have known kind of where to go next.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道接下来该怎么做。

sentences.en: Spikes isn't the only set of guidelines for breaking bad news,
sentences.zh: SPIKES并不是告知坏消息的唯一指导方针，

sentences.en: and it may not apply to every bad news situation.
sentences.zh: 它可能并不适用于所有告知坏消息的情况。

sentences.en: In some scenarios, like in an emergency room, doctors might not have the time to be that delicate.
sentences.zh: 在某些场景下，比如急诊室，医生可能没有时间表现得那么委婉。

sentences.en: And time is one of the main things working against doctors as they try to do their jobs thoroughly and compassionately.
sentences.zh: 时间是医生在试图彻底且富有同情心地完成工作时，所面临的主要阻碍之一。

sentences.en: These days, the average physician visit lasts about 21 minutes.
sentences.zh: 如今，平均每次医生门诊持续约21分钟。

sentences.en: More than half of visits last 15 minutes or less.
sentences.zh: 超过一半的门诊时间在15分钟或更短。

sentences.en: It can be really stressful to try to convey necessary information in that amount of time,
sentences.zh: 试图在这么短的时间内传达必要的信息真的压力很大，

sentences.en: especially if somebody is freaking out because, you know, they're dying.
sentences.zh: 尤其是如果有人因为意识到自己快要死了而惊慌失措时。

sentences.en: And throughout the course of their careers,
sentences.zh: 在整个职业生涯中，

sentences.en: many doctors will have to break bad news over and over and over again.
sentences.zh: 许多医生不得不一次又一次地告知坏消息。

sentences.en: It's emotionally exhausting.
sentences.zh: 这在情感上令人筋疲力尽。

sentences.en: Spikes helps doctors do what they need to do in the limited time they have.
sentences.zh: SPIKES帮助医生在有限的时间内完成他们需要做的事情。

sentences.en: It turns the awful task of breaking bad news into a clear and simple set of steps.
sentences.zh: 它将告知坏消息这项可怕的任务变成了一套清晰简单的步骤。

sentences.en: What it really is, is a protocol that can help doctors be more like Rob,
sentences.zh: 它实际上是一套可以帮助医生变得更像罗伯的方案，

sentences.en: or at least the person he tried to be.
sentences.zh: 或者至少像他努力成为的那种人。

sentences.en: Open, honest, and empathetic.
sentences.zh: 开放、诚实且富有同情心。

sentences.en: Here's John Cleese again.
sentences.zh: 约翰·克里斯又来了。

sentences.en: I think it takes empathy.
sentences.zh: 我认为这需要同理心。

sentences.en: How can you talk to someone, whether it's a group of people or a single person,
sentences.zh: 你怎么能和别人交谈，无论是一群人还是一个人，

sentences.en: how can you talk to them if you don't have an empathetic feeling of basically who they are,
sentences.zh: 如果你没有一种共情的感觉，去理解他们本质上是谁，

sentences.en: what they know already, and what they need to know?
sentences.zh: 他们已经知道了什么，以及他们需要知道什么，你又怎么能和他们交谈呢？

sentences.en: Rob's funeral was held in Toronto.
sentences.zh: 罗伯的葬礼在多伦多举行。

sentences.en: The same minister who married Rob and Pat led the service.
sentences.zh: 为罗伯和帕特主持婚礼的同一位牧师主持了仪式。

sentences.en: Before Rob died, he requested that this song be played as people exited.
sentences.zh: 罗伯去世前，要求在人们离场时播放这首歌。

sentences.en: What a day for a daydream.
sentences.zh: 多么适合白日梦的一天。

sentences.en: What a day for a daydreaming boy.
sentences.zh: 多么适合白日梦男孩的一天。

sentences.en: At my funeral service, I want to record a message which is played as the people are leaving.
sentences.zh: 在我的葬礼上，我想录一段留言，在人们离开时播放。

sentences.en: And it's just me, and I'm going to say,
sentences.zh: 只有我一个人，我会说，

sentences.en: thank you so much for coming.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们的到来。

sentences.en: Unlike the rest of you, I don't have to get up in the morning.
sentences.zh: 不像你们其他人，我早上不用起床了。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: That message wasn't actually played at Rob's funeral, even though he joked that he wanted it to be.
sentences.zh: 那段留言实际上并没有在罗伯的葬礼上播放，尽管他曾开玩笑说他希望播放它。

sentences.en: But you'll hear more from Rob and from Monty Python's John Cleese right after this.
sentences.zh: 但稍后你将听到更多关于罗伯和蒙提·派森成员约翰·克里斯的内容。

sentences.en: So I'm back with reporter John Fasile to talk about some of the remarkable,
sentences.zh: 我又和记者约翰·法西尔在一起，谈论一些非凡的、

sentences.en: heretofore pretty much unseen comedy that he found while he was reporting on Rob Buckman.
sentences.zh: 此前几乎未曾公开的喜剧内容，这是他在报道罗伯·巴克曼时发现的。

sentences.en: But we couldn't fit it into the story itself, so this is a little extra bit for you Monty Python fans.
sentences.zh: 但我们无法将其放入故事本身，所以这是给蒙提·派森粉丝的一点额外内容。

sentences.en: So, Roman, are you a Monty Python fan?
sentences.zh: 那么，罗曼，你是蒙提·派森的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: I would say I went through a Monty Python phase.
sentences.zh: 我会说我经历过一个蒙提·派森阶段。

sentences.en: A phase?
sentences.zh: 一个阶段？

sentences.en: A phase, you know, like in junior high where you find them and you think,
sentences.zh: 一个阶段，你知道，就像在初中时，你发现了他们，然后心想，

sentences.en: I'm really special for liking this when no one else liked it because it was just on PBS.
sentences.zh: 因为只有公共电视网（PBS）在播，没人看，所以我喜欢他们显得我很特别。

sentences.en: That was my phase where I watched all of them and loved them, but I haven't kept my fandom alive.
sentences.zh: 那是我观看并喜爱他们所有作品的阶段，但我并没有保持这种粉丝热情。

sentences.en: So, like, I'm a huge Monty Python fan, and when I started reporting the story,
sentences.zh: 所以，我是蒙提·派森的超级粉丝，当我开始报道这个故事时，

sentences.en: I had no idea there was any connection between Rob and Monty Python.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道罗伯和蒙提·派森之间有什么联系。

sentences.en: So finding that out was, like, a big deal.
sentences.zh: 所以发现这一点真是件大事。

sentences.en: And then I also, you know, found all this rare stuff that hardly anybody has seen,
sentences.zh: 然后我还发现了所有这些几乎没人见过的珍稀素材，

sentences.en: like stuff I got from tapes that Rob's widow pulled out of storage.
sentences.zh: 比如我从罗伯遗孀从仓库里找出的磁带中得到的素材。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so cool.
sentences.zh: 噢，那太酷了。

sentences.en: Like what?
sentences.zh: 比如什么？

sentences.en: Give me an example.
sentences.zh: 给我举个例子。

sentences.en: Well, so right around the time Rob was writing How to Break Bad News in the early 90s,
sentences.zh: 嗯，就在90年代初罗伯撰写《如何告知坏消息》的时候，

sentences.en: John Cleese got in touch with him,
sentences.zh: 约翰·克里斯联系了他，

sentences.en: and he had this idea for a series called Videos for Patients.
sentences.zh: 他有一个关于制作名为《患者视频》系列的构想。

sentences.en: I said it always seemed to me that it would be a very good idea to make videos
sentences.zh: 我说过，在我看来，制作视频总是一个非常好的主意。

sentences.en: for people who had just been told by their GP that they had some sort of medical problem,
sentences.zh: 针对那些刚被全科医生告知患有某种疾病的患者，

sentences.en: because when you're told that, you always get anxious,
sentences.zh: 因为当你听到这种消息时，总是会感到焦虑，

sentences.en: and that is absolutely the worst time to take in information.
sentences.zh: 而那绝对是接收信息最糟糕的时机。

sentences.en: The idea was to make a bunch of videos describing various medical conditions in detail
sentences.zh: 最初的想法是制作一系列视频，详细描述各种医疗状况，

sentences.en: so that patients with those conditions could replay them whenever they needed a refresher.
sentences.zh: 这样患者在需要复习时就可以随时重看。

sentences.en: And almost all of them start with this little sketch that kind of spoofs breaking bad news.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有视频都以一个小短剧开头，算是对“告知坏消息”的一种戏仿。

sentences.en: And some very beautiful music.
sentences.zh: 还有一些非常美妙的音乐。

sentences.en: 90s CD-ROM music.
sentences.zh: 90年代CD-ROM风格的音乐。

sentences.en: All right, doctor, what's my problem?
sentences.zh: 好吧，医生，我有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: Well, you've got leg ulcers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你患有腿部溃疡。

sentences.en: Leg ulcers.
sentences.zh: 腿部溃疡。

sentences.en: So, Cleese plays a patient inquiring about his condition,
sentences.zh: 所以，克里斯扮演一名询问自己病情的患者，

sentences.en: and Rob, the doctor, proceeds to lay some heavy medical jargon on him.
sentences.zh: 而罗布医生则开始对他抛出一堆深奥的医学术语。

sentences.en: I see.
sentences.zh: 我明白了。

sentences.en: What exactly are leg ulcers?
sentences.zh: 腿部溃疡到底是什么？

sentences.en: Well, quite simply, a leg ulcer is the consequence of tissue hypoxia,
sentences.zh: 嗯，简单来说，腿部溃疡是组织缺氧的结果，

sentences.en: following on ischemia due to venous stasis,
sentences.zh: 继发于静脉淤滞导致的缺血，

sentences.en: evidenced by proximal varicosities and incompetent perforators,
sentences.zh: 表现为近端静脉曲张和穿通支功能不全，

sentences.en: or, of course, due to arterial insufficiency.
sentences.zh: 当然，也可能是由于动脉供血不足引起的。

sentences.en: There's full thickness epidermal...
sentences.zh: 有全层表皮……

sentences.en: So, as Rob's talking, the camera slowly zooms in on Cleese,
sentences.zh: 所以，当罗布在说话时，摄像机缓慢地推向克里斯，

sentences.en: who looks increasingly confused and upset.
sentences.zh: 他看起来越来越困惑和不安。

sentences.en: He leans in, squints, looks over his shoulder.
sentences.zh: 他探过身子，眯起眼睛，回头看了看。

sentences.en: By the time the camera lands in close-up,
sentences.zh: 当镜头最终推进到特写时，

sentences.en: his face is slack, and his eyes are wide with terror.
sentences.zh: 他的脸松弛下来，双眼因恐惧而睁大。

sentences.en: Are there any questions?
sentences.zh: 还有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Are you sure?
sentences.zh: 你确定吗？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 确定。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Then I'll see you in six weeks.
sentences.zh: 那六周后再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Then Cleese gets up and walks off stage,
sentences.zh: 然后克里斯起身走下舞台，

sentences.en: revealing to the audience that he's on a set.
sentences.zh: 向观众揭示他正身处摄影棚中。

sentences.en: As it happens, I haven't got a leg ulcer.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我并没有腿部溃疡。

sentences.en: And, of course, doctors don't really talk like that.
sentences.zh: 当然，医生们平时说话并不是那样。

sentences.en: Although sometimes it can feel a bit as though they do.
sentences.zh: 尽管有时听起来确实有点像那样。

sentences.en: By the time I get home,
sentences.zh: 等我回到家时，

sentences.en: I always realize that I haven't understood everything that the doctors said,
sentences.zh: 我总是意识到自己并没有完全听懂医生说的一切，

sentences.en: and that there are always some questions that I should have asked,
sentences.zh: 而且总有一些我本该问的问题，

sentences.en: but for some reason didn't.
sentences.zh: 但出于某种原因没问出口。

sentences.en: And that's exactly why we've made this video.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们制作这个视频的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, so then the rest of the video is just Rob going over the condition
sentences.zh: 没错，视频剩下的部分就是罗布在讲解病情，

sentences.en: slowly and in painstaking detail.
sentences.zh: 讲得非常缓慢且细致入微。

sentences.en: A leg ulcer is what happens when the skin over a part of your leg can't grow properly.
sentences.zh: 腿部溃疡是当你的腿部某处皮肤无法正常生长时发生的情况。

sentences.en: They made almost 50 of these videos on everything from breast cancer
sentences.zh: 他们制作了近50个这样的视频，涵盖了从乳腺癌

sentences.en: to something called glue ear, which I've never heard of.
sentences.zh: 到一种叫“胶耳”的病，我以前从没听说过。

sentences.en: But they ran into a problem.
sentences.zh: 但他们遇到了一个问题。

sentences.en: But we hit a major problem which none of us had anticipated,
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了一个我们都没预料到的重大问题，

sentences.en: and I'm not entirely sure one could have anticipated it.
sentences.zh: 而且我不确定有人能预料到这一点。

sentences.en: What was the problem?
sentences.zh: 是什么问题？

sentences.en: They had trouble selling them?
sentences.zh: 他们卖不出去？

sentences.en: Yeah, that makes sense.
sentences.zh: 是的，这说得通。

sentences.en: We set up all sorts of schemes, but we just couldn't really shift them.
sentences.zh: 我们制定了各种计划，但真的卖不动。

sentences.en: We could never find a way of getting people to give us 12 or 13 quid
sentences.zh: 我们始终找不到办法让人们愿意掏12或13英镑

sentences.en: for a 25-minute lecture.
sentences.zh: 去买一个25分钟的讲座。

sentences.en: People wouldn't pay.
sentences.zh: 人们不愿买单。

sentences.en: So that's why you've never seen them.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你从未见过它们的原因。

sentences.en: But now you can see them on our website.
sentences.zh: 但现在你可以在我们的网站上看到了。

sentences.en: Yes, you can.
sentences.zh: 是的，可以。

sentences.en: You can see one of those videos, and you can also see footage of Rob's strip routine
sentences.zh: 你可以看到其中一个视频，还可以看到罗布在“脚灯”剧团时期的脱衣舞表演片段，

sentences.en: from the Footlights days and the stuff he did with Terry Jones.
sentences.zh: 以及他与特里·琼斯合作的内容。

sentences.en: Right, so Rob Buckman also worked on some videos with another member of Monty Python,
sentences.zh: 没错，罗布·巴克曼还与另一位“蒙提·派森”成员合作过一些视频，

sentences.en: Terry Jones.
sentences.zh: 特里·琼斯。

sentences.en: Can you tell me a little bit about those?
sentences.zh: 能跟我讲讲那些视频吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was literally the last thing he ever did.
sentences.zh: 是的，那真的是他做的最后一件事。

sentences.en: He died on the plane on the way back from working with Terry in London.
sentences.zh: 他在从伦敦与特里工作回来的飞机上去世了。

sentences.en: And these videos you can see online already.
sentences.zh: 这些视频你现在可以在网上看到。

sentences.en: They're called the Top 10 Tips for Health.
sentences.zh: 它们叫《健康十大贴士》。

sentences.en: The goal was to provide practical tips for staying healthy,
sentences.zh: 目标是提供保持健康的实用建议，

sentences.en: although really when you're watching it,
sentences.zh: 尽管当你观看时，

sentences.en: it just feels like you're watching two old men goof off.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像在看两个老头在胡闹。

sentences.en: Here's Rob and Terry in drag as two old ladies.
sentences.zh: 这是罗布和特里扮成两个老太太的样子。

sentences.en: Did you recognize the spam lady voice, Roman?
sentences.zh: 罗曼，你认出那个“垃圾邮件女士”的声音了吗？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 认出来了。

sentences.en: Also, this reminds me of one of my favorite sketches from the show,
sentences.zh: 另外，这让我想起了节目中我最喜欢的短剧之一，

sentences.en: which is like, hello, Mrs. Smoker.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你好，吸烟太太。

sentences.en: Hello, Mrs. Non-Smoker.
sentences.zh: 你好，不吸烟太太。

sentences.en: Been shopping?
sentences.zh: 去购物了吗？

sentences.en: No, been shopping.
sentences.zh: 没有，去购物了。

sentences.en: What'd you buy?
sentences.zh: 你买了什么？

sentences.en: A piston engine.
sentences.zh: 一台活塞发动机。

sentences.en: What'd you buy that for?
sentences.zh: 你买那个干什么？

sentences.en: It was a bargain.
sentences.zh: 那是捡了大便宜。

sentences.en: Anyway, that one I know by heart.
sentences.zh: 总之，那个短剧我倒背如流。

sentences.en: Oh, man, that was good.
sentences.zh: 天哪，那太棒了。

sentences.en: So there was in another sketch in that video series,
sentences.zh: 在那个视频系列中还有另一个短剧，

sentences.en: they actually directly make fun of breaking bad news.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上直接拿“告知坏消息”开涮。

sentences.en: I'm afraid you've got type 2 diabetes.
sentences.zh: 恐怕你得了2型糖尿病。

sentences.en: Well, isn't that nice?
sentences.zh: 嗯，那不是挺好的吗？

sentences.en: I'm sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉。

sentences.en: I said you have got type 2 diabetes, Mr. Robinson.
sentences.zh: 我说你得了2型糖尿病，罗宾逊先生。

sentences.en: I think I saw it in the cinema the other day.
sentences.zh: 我记得前几天在电影院看到过这个。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: Diabetes 2?
sentences.zh: 《糖尿病2》？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: So Terry Jones is still alive, but unfortunately, he's suffering from dementia,
sentences.zh: 所以特里·琼斯还活着，但不幸的是，他患有痴呆症，

sentences.en: so we weren't able to interview him.
sentences.zh: 所以我们没能采访他。

sentences.en: He and Rob were really close, though.
sentences.zh: 不过他和罗布真的很亲近。

sentences.en: Terry actually wrote Rob's obituary in The Guardian after he died.
sentences.zh: 罗布去世后，特里甚至在《卫报》上为他写了讣告。

sentences.en: I remember when you were putting the story together, when you got the interview with John
sentences.zh: 我记得当你筹备这个故事，拿到约翰·克里斯的采访时，

sentences.en: Cleese, I was just shocked, A, that he was involved, and B, that he talked to you.
sentences.zh: 我非常震惊，一是没想到他会参与，二是没想到他会接受你的采访。

sentences.en: How hard was that to manage?
sentences.zh: 这事儿办起来有多难？

sentences.en: Oh, man.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So I actually got that interview through Rob's daughter, Jo.
sentences.zh: 其实我是通过罗布的女儿乔联系到那个采访的。

sentences.en: Jo Buckman is a screenwriter in Los Angeles, and she participated in the interview, too.
sentences.zh: 乔·巴克曼是洛杉矶的一名编剧，她也参与了采访。

sentences.en: I think it meant a lot to her.
sentences.zh: 我想这对她意义重大。

sentences.en: You know, Rob's death was so sudden that I kind of got the sense from his family that
sentences.zh: 你知道，罗布去世得太突然了，我从他家人那里感觉到，

sentences.en: the wounds have never fully healed.
sentences.zh: 伤口从未完全愈合。

sentences.en: So for Jo, the chance to hear John Cleese talk about her dad in such glowing terms, I think
sentences.zh: 所以对乔来说，能听到约翰·克里斯用如此赞美的话语谈论她的父亲，我想

sentences.en: it was really meaningful for her.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有意义。

sentences.en: And it felt really good to be there and to hear that.
sentences.zh: 能在现场听到这些，感觉真的很棒。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's so nice.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: I'm so glad that that happened.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴这件事发生了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Rob's family has been really great and supportive of this story, but particularly Jo.
sentences.zh: 罗布的家人一直非常棒，很支持这个故事，尤其是乔。

sentences.en: She was really my partner in crime, you know, helping me with the Cleese interview, which
sentences.zh: 她真的是我的得力助手，你知道，帮我促成了克里斯的采访，这

sentences.en: is obviously a get, and then also helping me get some of the archival you heard in the
sentences.zh: 显然是个大收获，然后还帮我获取了你在故事中听到的部分档案资料。

sentences.en: story.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh, that's so great.
sentences.zh: 好吧，感谢乔·巴克曼的所有帮助。
